# Quest Board — Backend

Elysia REST API for the Quest Board challenge: an Nx monorepo with Bun as runtime, package manager and test
runner.

## Stack

- [Bun](https://bun.com/) — runtime, package manager, test runner
- [Elysia](https://elysiajs.com/) — HTTP framework
- [Drizzle](https://orm.drizzle.team/) — ORM (PostgreSQL)
- [Zod](https://zod.dev/) — request/response validation
- [Nx](https://nx.dev/) — monorepo task orchestration

## Setup

```bash
docker compose up -d --wait                         # start the dev + test Postgres containers
bun install                                         # install dependencies for every app/package
cp .env.sample .env                                 # root env: database URL
cp apps/rest-server/.env.sample apps/rest-server/.env   # API env: port, logs, docs, CORS
bun run migrate                                     # apply migrations to the dev database
bun run migrate:test                                # apply migrations to the test database
```

The `.env` files are not versioned; the `.env.sample` files next to them are the starting point. `loadEnv`
(in `@repo/env`) reads the root file first, then lets the app's own file override it, and validates the
result against the app's Zod schema (`apps/rest-server/src/env/env-schema.ts`). Tests use the versioned
`test.env` files instead.

Run the server:

```bash
bun run dev
```

The API is served under `/api/v1`. With `OPEN_API_SCHEMA_VISIBLE=true` (the default in `.env`/`test.env`),
the OpenAPI docs are at `/api/v1/docs`.

`ERROR_DETAILS_VISIBLE=true` adds field-level `details` to validation (422) and unknown-route (404) errors.
Keep it off outside dev/test. Unexpected (500) errors never expose details in the response: look them up in
the log by the `uuid` the response carries.

`CORS_ORIGINS` is a comma-separated list of the origins allowed to call the API from a browser. It defaults to
`http://localhost:4000`, the web app's dev server.

# Quest Board — Frontend

React/Vite web app for the Quest Board challenge: a single-screen quest board consuming the backend REST
API from `apps/rest-server`. Built on Taqtile's internal React Web template (design system, tooling
conventions), with the GraphQL/Firebase/auth pieces of that template removed — this app talks to a plain
REST API.

## Stack

- [Vite](https://vite.dev/) — dev server and bundler
- [React](https://react.dev/) + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
- [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) + `tailwind-variants` — styling

## Setup

Follow the setup in the root [`README.md`](README.md#how-to-run-the-project): it installs the dependencies
of every app (`bun install` at the repo root) and creates `apps/web/.env` from its sample. That file points
the app at the API:

```bash
# apps/web/.env
VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
```

```bash
bun run dev                      # from the repo root: starts the API (3000) and the web app (4000) together

```

connection error.


```bash
bun run typecheck                # tsc -b
```

args.newString:
A 3-column kanban board (Pergaminhos Novos / Em Jornada / Lendas Concluídas), one column per real quest
status, with a modal to create new quests. Moving a quest between columns persists its status through
`PATCH /quests/:id`, and quests can be edited from the board through the same endpoint. Difficulty is
chosen when creating a quest (`easy`, `normal` or `high`, defaulting to `normal`); the XP reward is
read-only, derived by the backend from the chosen difficulty.

# Quest Board — Backend

Elysia REST API for the Quest Board challenge: an Nx monorepo with Bun as runtime, package manager and test
runner.

## Stack

- [Bun](https://bun.com/) — runtime, package manager, test runner
- [Elysia](https://elysiajs.com/) — HTTP framework
- [Drizzle](https://orm.drizzle.team/) — ORM (PostgreSQL)
- [Zod](https://zod.dev/) — request/response validation
- [Nx](https://nx.dev/) — monorepo task orchestration

## Setup

```bash
docker compose up -d --wait                         # start the dev + test Postgres containers
bun install                                         # install dependencies for every app/package
cp .env.sample .env                                 # root env: database URL
cp apps/rest-server/.env.sample apps/rest-server/.env   # API env: port, logs, docs, CORS
bun run migrate                                     # apply migrations to the dev database
bun run migrate:test                                # apply migrations to the test database
```

The `.env` files are not versioned; the `.env.sample` files next to them are the starting point. `loadEnv`
(in `@repo/env`) reads the root file first, then lets the app's own file override it, and validates the
result against the app's Zod schema (`apps/rest-server/src/env/env-schema.ts`). Tests use the versioned
`test.env` files instead.

Run the server:

```bash
bun run dev
```

The API is served under `/api/v1`. With `OPEN_API_SCHEMA_VISIBLE=true` (the default in `.env`/`test.env`),
the OpenAPI docs are at `/api/v1/docs`.

`ERROR_DETAILS_VISIBLE=true` adds field-level `details` to validation (422) and unknown-route (404) errors.

the log by the `uuid` the response carries.

`http://localhost:4000`, the web app's dev server.

# Quest Board — Frontend

React/Vite web app for the Quest Board challenge: a single-screen quest board consuming the backend REST
API from `apps/rest-server`. Built on Taqtile's internal React Web template (design system, tooling
conventions), with the GraphQL/Firebase/auth pieces of that template removed — this app talks to a plain
REST API.

## Stack

- [Vite](https://vite.dev/) — dev server and bundler
- [React](https://react.dev/) + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
- [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) + `tailwind-variants` — styling
- `src/atomic/` — Taqtile's Atomic Design system (Button, text inputs, Typography, Modal, Grid, Loading...)
- [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/) + Testing Library — unit/component tests
- [Storybook](https://storybook.js.org/) — isolated component development

## Setup

Follow the setup in the root [`README.md`](README.md#how-to-run-the-project): it installs the dependencies
of every app (`bun install` at the repo root) and creates `apps/web/.env` from its sample. That file points
the app at the API:

```bash
# apps/web/.env
VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
```

## Running

```bash
bun run dev                      # from the repo root: starts the API (3000) and the web app (4000) together
bunx nx dev @repo/web            # from the repo root: just the web app, at http://localhost:4000
```

Running the web app alone only makes sense when the API is already running: without it, the board shows a
connection error.

## Testing

```bash
bunx nx test @repo/web           # from the repo root
# or, from apps/web/:
bun run test                     # Vitest
bun run storybook                # isolated component development, http://localhost:6006
```

## Code quality

```bash
bun run typecheck                # tsc -b
```

Lint/format run through the same root-level `oxlint`/`oxfmt` as the backend (`bun run lint` at the repo
root). `src/atomic/` and `.storybook/` are excluded from both — that's Taqtile's own design-system templat… [truncated, 2122 more chars]

<task_result>
## Backend conventions (quests feature)

### Not found
- **Error type**: `NotFoundError` from `@repo/core/error` (`packages/core/src/error/not-found.error.ts`) → HTTP 404, BaseError subclass.
- **Domain error code**: `QuestErrors.NotFound = { code: 'QST_01', message: 'Missão não encontrada.' }` (`apps/rest-server/src/domain/quests/quests.error.ts:2`).
- **Use cases**: `GetQuestUseCase.exec` (get-quest.use-case.ts:9-13) and `UpdateQuestUseCase.exec` (update-quest.use-case.ts:9-17) call `QuestsDbDatasource.findOneById`; throw `NotFoundError(QuestErrors.NotFound)` when null. Update checks existence twice (before + after update).
- **Datasource**: `findOneById` filters `deletedAt: { isNull: true }` (quests.db.datasource.ts:34-36), so soft-deleted rows are treated as not found.
- **Controller**: GET `/:id` and PATCH `/:id` declare `404: 'ErrorsResponse'` (quests.controller.ts:28,52). Error middleware maps BaseError → its status/code/message + uuid (error.middleware.ts).

### Deletion
- **No delete endpoint/use case exists.** Deletion is soft-only via `deletedAt` nullable timestamp column (`packages/db/src/schema/quests.entity.ts:20`).
- Active reads filter `isNull(questTable.deletedAt)` everywhere (datasource.ts:35,47,58,82).
- Seeds support `deletedAt` input (quests.seed.ts); tests verify deleted quests → 404 on PATCH (quests-id.patch.test.ts "should give a 404 error if the quest is deleted").
- DB reset between tests uses `clearDatabase()` TRUNCATE (packages/db/test/clear-database.utils.ts).

### Validation
- Zod schemas in `apps/rest-server/src/api/quests/quests.payload.ts`: `QuestRequest` (lines 28-32), `QuestUpdateRequest` (34-39), `QuestParams` id `startsWith('q_')` (41-43), `QuestsQuery` extends `PageRequest` + optional status (45-47).
- Rules: title/description trim/min(1)/max; difficulty enum with `.default('normal').catch('normal')` on create (line 31) so invalid values fall back to norm… [truncated, 1881 more chars]

# Quest Board — Backend

Elysia REST API for the Quest Board challenge: an Nx monorepo with Bun as runtime, package manager and test
runner.

## Stack

- [Bun](https://bun.com/) — runtime, package manager, test runner
- [Elysia](https://elysiajs.com/) — HTTP framework
- [Drizzle](https://orm.drizzle.team/) — ORM (PostgreSQL)
- [Zod](https://zod.dev/) — request/response validation
- [Nx](https://nx.dev/) — monorepo task orchestration

## Setup

```bash
docker compose up -d --wait                         # start the dev + test Postgres containers
bun install                                         # install dependencies for every app/package
cp .env.sample .env                                 # root env: database URL
cp apps/rest-server/.env.sample apps/rest-server/.env   # API env: port, logs, docs, CORS
bun run migrate                                     # apply migrations to the dev database
bun run migrate:test                                # apply migrations to the test database
```

The `.env` files are not versioned; the `.env.sample` files next to them are the starting point. `loadEnv`
(in `@repo/env`) reads the root file first, then lets the app's own file override it, and validates the
result against the app's Zod schema (`apps/rest-server/src/env/env-schema.ts`). Tests use the versioned
`test.env` files instead.

Run the server:

```bash
bun run dev
```

The API is served under `/api/v1`. With `OPEN_API_SCHEMA_VISIBLE=true` (the default in `.env`/`test.env`),
the OpenAPI docs are at `/api/v1/docs`.

`ERROR_DETAILS_VISIBLE=true` adds field-level `details` to validation (422) and unknown-route (404) errors.
Keep it off outside dev/test. Unexpected (500) errors never expose details in the response: look them up in
the log by the `uuid` the response carries.

`CORS_ORIGINS` is a comma-separated list of the origins allowed to call the API from a browser. It defaults to
`http://localhost:4000`, the web app's dev server.

questions.question: Should the due date be a date-only value or a full timestamp?

options.label: Date-only (Recommended)
options.description: Postgres `date` column; API uses `YYYY-MM-DD`. Native date input gives a calendar and avoids timezone off-by-one bugs.

options.label: Timestamp
options.description: Postgres `timestamptz`; API uses ISO datetime. More precise, but the date input must convert to/from local time.

questions.question: Should resolved quests still be highlighted when their due date has passed?

options.label: No, only active (Recommended)
options.description: Only open/in-progress quests count as overdue; resolved quests show the date without a warning highlight.

options.label: Yes, any past date
options.description: Highlight every quest whose due date is in the past, even if resolved.

questions.question: When duplicating a quest, should the copy keep the original due date?

options.label: Yes, copy it (Recommended)
options.description: Due date is user-authored editable data, so the duplicate starts with the same date and can be changed.

options.label: No, leave it empty
options.description: The duplicate starts without a due date, forcing the user to choose a new one.

`POST /quests`, `PATCH /quests/:id` and `DELETE /quests/:id` — see
[`apps/rest-server/src/api/quests/`](apps/rest-server/src/api/quests/).

Quests have an optional, nullable `due_date` column. The API exposes it as `dueDate` in the date-only
`YYYY-MM-DD` format. `POST /quests` accepts an omitted or `null` value, and `PATCH /quests/:id` accepts
`null` to clear an existing due date; invalid dates are rejected with `422`.

difficulty. The XP bar reflects the sum of the XP rewards of resolved quests: every 100 XP is a new
level, and the bar shows progress within the current level.

browser calendar and can be left empty. Active quests whose due date is before today are highlighted on
the card with an "Atrasada" badge; resolved quests are never highlighted. Dates are handled as
`YYYY-MM-DD` strings to avoid timezone shifts.

questions.question: Which IDs should the quest_tag junction table reference?

options.label: External IDs (Recommended)
options.description: Join on quest.id (q_...) and tag.id (t_...). Matches the requested composite key directly and keeps API/DB mapping simple.

options.label: Internal IDs
options.description: Join on quest.internalId and tag.internalId integer keys. More conventional and compact, but requires extra mapping in queries.

questions.question: How should tag filtering work?

options.label: Client-side (Recommended)
options.description: Quests already return their tags; the board filters them locally like the difficulty filter. No new query parameter.

options.label: Server-side query
options.description: Add a `tags` query parameter to GET /quests and filter in SQL. More scalable, but adds API/query complexity.

questions.question: How should users enter tags in the create/edit forms?

options.label: Chip input (Recommended)
options.description: Type a tag and press Enter/comma to add a removable chip; supports empty state and keyboard removal.

options.label: Comma-separated field
options.description: One text field where tags are separated by commas. Simpler, but less polished.

questions.question: When several tags are selected in the filter, which quests should appear?

options.label: Any selected tag (Recommended)
options.description: OR semantics: show quests that have at least one selected tag.

options.label: All selected tags
options.description: AND semantics: show only quests that have every selected tag.

# Quest Board — Taqtile Challenge

## About

This project is an incomplete fullstack Quest Board application (backend API + React frontend) with a fantasy RPG theme: quests, each with a difficulty and an XP reward. Your task is to complete the missing pieces, connecting both layers.

The main purpose of this challenge is not to evaluate your prior knowledge of any specific framework, but to show us how you solve a problem, how you study for it, and how you use AI tools as part of your workflow.

Think of this challenge as your first task working at Taqtile: what you deliver here is what we would expect from your work in a real project given the same constraints.

questions.question: What should “delete an existing tag” do?

options.label: Delete globally (Recommended)
options.description: Remove the tag from the catalog and from every quest that uses it, after a confirmation step.

options.label: Remove from quest only
options.description: Unlink the tag from the current quest but keep it in the catalog for other quests.

options.label: Both actions
options.description: Let users unlink a tag from this quest and separately delete the tag from the catalog globally.

questions.question: How should the quest forms submit selected tags?

options.label: Tag IDs via /tags API (Recommended)
options.description: Add GET/POST/DELETE /tags endpoints; quests send tagIds. Cleaner for selecting existing tags and avoids name ambiguity.

options.label: Tag names via quest API
options.description: Keep quests sending tag names, with GET /tags only for suggestions. New tags can be created through the quest update.

questions.question: How should tag names that differ only by case be handled?

options.label: Reuse ignoring case (Recommended)
options.description: Store the first spelling exactly as entered, but treat “Urgente” and “urgente” as the same catalog tag.

options.label: Treat as separate tags
options.description: Preserve exact names and allow “Urgente” and “urgente” to exist as distinct tags.

questions.question: Where should the tag catalog be available?

options.label: Both forms, manage in edit (Recommended)
options.description: Create and edit forms can select existing tags or create new ones; deletion is available only in the edit form.

options.label: Edit form only
options.description: Tags can only be added or removed after the quest is created.

options.label: Full management in both forms
options.description: Create and edit forms both allow selecting, creating, and deleting catalog tags.

# Quest Board — Backend

Elysia REST API for the Quest Board challenge: an Nx monorepo with Bun as runtime, package manager and test
runner.

## Stack

- [Bun](https://bun.com/) — runtime, package manager, test runner
- [Elysia](https://elysiajs.com/) — HTTP framework
- [Drizzle](https://orm.drizzle.team/) — ORM (PostgreSQL)
- [Zod](https://zod.dev/) — request/response validation
- [Nx](https://nx.dev/) — monorepo task orchestration

## Setup

```bash
docker compose up -d --wait                         # start the dev + test Postgres containers
bun install                                         # install dependencies for every app/package
cp .env.sample .env                                 # root env: database URL
cp apps/rest-server/.env.sample apps/rest-server/.env   # API env: port, logs, docs, CORS
bun run migrate                                     # apply migrations to the dev database
bun run migrate:test                                # apply migrations to the test database
```

The `.env` files are not versioned; the `.env.sample` files next to them are the starting point. `loadEnv`
(in `@repo/env`) reads the root file first, then lets the app's own file override it, and validates the
result against the app's Zod schema (`apps/rest-server/src/env/env-schema.ts`). Tests use the versioned
`test.env` files instead.

Run the server:

```bash
bun run dev
```

The API is served under `/api/v1`. With `OPEN_API_SCHEMA_VISIBLE=true` (the default in `.env`/`test.env`),
the OpenAPI docs are at `/api/v1/docs`.

`ERROR_DETAILS_VISIBLE=true` adds field-level `details` to validation (422) and unknown-route (404) errors.
Keep it off outside dev/test. Unexpected (500) errors never expose details in the response: look them up in
the log by the `uuid` the response carries.

`CORS_ORIGINS` is a comma-separated list of the origins allowed to call the API from a browser. It defaults to
`http://localhost:4000`, the web app's dev server.

## Tags feature

Tags are a global catalog managed by `GET /tags`, `POST /tags` and `DELETE /tags/:id` — see
[`apps/rest-server/src/api/tags/`](apps/rest-server/src/api/tags/). A quest references tags through the
`quest_tag` join table, and every quest response includes its `tags` sorted by display name.

```http
POST /api/v1/tags
Content-Type: application/json

{ "name": "Dragão" }
```

Tag display names are stored exactly as entered after trimming. Identity is case-insensitive: the API
stores a normalized name (`trim().normalize('NFC').toLocaleLowerCase('pt-BR')`) with a unique constraint,
so `POST /tags` returns `409` with code `TAG_02` when the normalized name already exists. Tag names are
limited to 30 characters.

Quest create/update payloads accept an optional `tagIds` array (maximum 10 IDs). Invalid or unknown tag
IDs are rejected with `422` and code `QST_02`. Sending `tagIds: []` to `PATCH /quests/:id` clears the
quest's tags; omitting `tagIds` leaves them unchanged. Deleting a tag from the catalog cascades through
`quest_tag`, removing it from every quest.
EOF
